scopes.exact_span: D02 gives locally uniform absolute convergence and holomorphy of the integral on \(\Re s>27/32\): the finite part ending at \(e^{200}\) is entire and the tail is bounded on compacta by integrals of \(t^{-1-\epsilon}\log^2t/64\). Uniqueness of meromorphic continuation excludes a zero there (a zero of multiplicity (m) gives a nonremovable pole with residue (-m)). There is no assertion about the boundary. This inference uses the exact exponent, while the coefficient and onset ensure integrability and need not occur in the new density constants. This is the reason a conditional improvement need not wait for \(x=e^{200}\). The direct pointwise error bound itself is used **only** on its stated domain. Set \(\beta=7/8\) or \(27/32\) according to the premise and \(a=1-\beta\). Nontrivial zeros are paired by conjugation and reflection in \(\Re s=1/2\); no real zero in \(0<s<1\) (the alternating \(\zeta\) series there has positive sum and (1-2^{1-s}\ne0)).

scopes.exact_span:
Let \(H=3\cdot10^{12}\), \(h=\log H\). All zeros with \(0<\gamma\le H\) lie on the critical line. For \(s\ge .745\), put \(p=8(1-s)/3, d=1-p, q=5-2s\). Here \(3<q<4\) for every band used. For \(Y\ge H\), the two applicable inequalities for \(N(s,Y)\) (positive ordinates, \(\Re\rho\ge s\), multiplicities) are \(A\,Y^p(\log Y)^q+B(\log Y)^2\), with
\[
 (A,B)=\big(4.9\,3^p, 51.5\big)\quad\text{or}\quad(c(s),5).
\]
The first is \(\log(1+z)\le z\) in Dusart 2.3; the second uses FKS Corollary 2.9. In increasing bands beginning at (.700,.750,.800,.810,.820,.830,.840,.850,.860,.870) take \(c(s)=6.1727,7.7979,8.2,8.6,9,9.4,9.8,10.2,10.7,11.1\), respectively, up to the next left endpoint (outward enlargements). At a shared endpoint the next band's bound is valid. These are cited as the *conclusion* of Corollary 2.9, not a recomputation of Theorem 2.7's optimization parameters. In particular there is a notation discrepancy involving the printed \(\delta\) range versus Table 8; the independent Dusart density can be selected by the `RAM_ONLY=1` replay. We do not use PT 2021's truncated formula \(7\) or FKS 3.1/Prop. 3.4 in the new proofs; FKS Remark 3.3 flags issues in the older truncated formulas.

For \(s\ge.745\), \(2\sum_{\Re\rho\ge s, \gamma\ge V}1/\gamma\), for \(V\ge H\) or \(V\) below \(H\) if the stated density bound is valid from \(V\), is bounded by \(2\int_V^\infty \widetilde N(s,y)y^{-2}dy\) using integration by parts, with no subtraction needed at the lower end. In uses with \(V<H\) below, simply use that the count is zero until \(H\), so the bound by a positive analytic majorant integrated from \(V\) is still valid. Counting \(\gamma=V\) is allowed. For \(V=H\) take the minimum of the two resulting upper bounds. With \(h=\log H\) one can majorize the integral of \(y^p(\log y)^q/y^2\) by
\[
 J_q = e^{-dh}h^q\sum_{j=0}^4 (q)_j/(h^j d^{j+1}).
\]
Indeed the degree-four Taylor polynomial of \((1+v)^q\) at zero is an upper bound for \(v\ge0\) (fifth derivative negative). The integral of \((\log y)^2/y^2\) is \((h^2+2h+2)/H\). Define \(C(s)=2\min(AJ_q+B(h^2+2h+2)/H)\) over the two densities. These constants need not be monotone as formulas across band edges; replacing each by the running minimum as \(s\) increases preserves the inequality.

For the mesh \(s_0=.745<s_1<\cdots<s_m=\beta\), take steps .001 up to the last endpoint (truncate the last step if necessary). Let \(C_i\) be the running minima through \(i\) for \(0\le i<m\), and set \(C_m=0\) **only as a notation for telescoping**, not a bound on the zeros at \(\beta\). Define
\[
 Z_\beta(u)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(C_i-C_{i+1})e^{-(1-s_{i+1})u}.
 \tag{Z}
\]
This bounds the absolute contribution of all high zeros \(\Re\rho\ge s_0\) to the relative explicit formula at \(e^u\). In fact each exponential \(e^{-(1-\Re\rho)u}\) is bounded by its right mesh endpoint plus the usual cumulative-level telescoping, including a zero precisely on the cap. This argument gives the alternative expression \(C_0 e^{-(1-s_0)u}+\sum_i C_i(e^{-(1-s_{i+1})u}-e^{-(1-s_i)u})\); from it reducing the cap decreases the bound. All positive sums are absolutely convergent.

scopes.exact_span:
For \(u\ge60\) use FKS \(3.2\) with \(x=e^u, T=e^{u/2}/6\), so \(T\le T^\star<e^{u/2}\) and the relative remainder is \(12.546 u e^{-u/2}\). This meets \(T<(e^{u/2}-2)/5\), \(T>\max(51,u)\), and the onset \(u\ge40\). Write
\[
 S=(u/2-1.83)^2/12.56+.933,\qquad
 J=((u/2-1.83)^2-26.88^2)/12.56+1.865,\qquad
 U=(12.546 u+2S)e^{-u/2}.
\]
By PT Lemma 2, \(S\) bounds the reciprocal sum over positive ordinates up to \(e^{u/2}\); \(J\) bounds it above \(H\). Use \(1.83<\log(2\pi)<1.84, \log H>28.72\). Conjugate zeros double the weight; the reflected zeros left of the line cost at most the line contribution. Off-line zeros on the right above height \(H\) consume at most half the reciprocal sum above \(H\) by reflection. Writing their excess via the mesh gives
\[
 |\psi(e^u)/e^u-1| \le b_\beta(u)
 = U+ (J-C_0)_+e^{-(1-s_0)u}+Z_\beta(u).
 \tag{B}
\]
Only the two caps are compared here. In particular both yield a decaying error with the corresponding power and no positive log factor. We also have all original applicable envelopes and, under \(B_1\), the direct \(u^2e^{-5u/32}/64\) at \(u\ge200\). For \(\theta\), add the prime-power relative bound
\[
 D_+(u)=1.000000147e^{-u/2}+1.78e^{-2u/3}
\]
from Dusart 4.5, and intersect with all direct \(\theta\) bounds. One may use the tighter signed interval \([-b-D_+, b-D_-]\), with \(0\le D_-\le(\psi-\theta)/x\) as in §5. These transformations never decrease the established domains. Below 60 no explicit-formula claim is made by (B).

For \(s\ge.745\), \(2\sum_{\Re\rho\ge s, \gamma\ge V}1/\gamma\), for \(V\ge H\) or \(V\) below \(H\) if the stated density bound is valid from \(V\), is bounded by \(2\int_V^\infty \widetilde N(s,y)y^{-2}dy\) using integration by parts, with no subtraction needed at the lower end. In uses with \(V<H\) below, simply use that the count is zero until \(H\), so the bound by a positive analytic majorant integrated from \(V\) is still valid. Counting \(\gamma=V\) is allowed. For \(V=H\) take the minimum of the two resulting upper bounds. With \(h=\log H\) one can majorize the integral of \(y^p(\log y)^q/y^2\) by
\[
 J_q = e^{-dh}h^q\sum_{j=0}^4 (q)_j/(h^j d^{j+1}).
\]
Indeed the degree-four Taylor polynomial of \((1+v)^q\) at zero is an upper bound for \(v\ge0\) (fifth derivative negative). The integral of \((\log y)^2/y^2\) is \((h^2+2h+2)/H\). Define \(C(s)=2\min(AJ_q+B(h^2+2h+2)/H)\) over the two densities. These constants need not be monotone as formulas across band edges; replacing each by the running minimum as \(s\) increases preserves the inequality.

For the mesh \(s_0=.745<s_1<\cdots<s_m=\beta\), take steps .001 up to the last endpoint (truncate the last step if necessary). Let \(C_i\) be the running minima through \(i\) for \(0\le i<m\), and set \(C_m=0\) **only as a notation for telescoping**, not a bound on the zeros at \(\beta\). Define
\[
 Z_\beta(u)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(C_i-C_{i+1})e^{-(1-s_{i+1})u}.
 \tag{Z}
\]
This bounds the absolute contribution of all high zeros \(\Re\rho\ge s_0\) to the relative explicit formula at \(e^u\). In fact each exponential \(e^{-(1-\Re\rho)u}\) is bounded by its right mesh endpoint plus the usual cumulative-level telescoping, including a zero precisely on the cap. This argument gives the alternative expression \(C_0 e^{-(1-s_0)u}+\sum_i C_i(e^{-(1-s_{i+1})u}-e^{-(1-s_i)u})\); from it reducing the cap decreases the bound. All positive sums are absolutely convergent.

\[
 S=(u/2-1.83)^2/12.56+.933,\qquad
 J=((u/2-1.83)^2-26.88^2)/12.56+1.865,\qquad
 U=(12.546 u+2S)e^{-u/2}.
\]
By PT Lemma 2, \(S\) bounds the reciprocal sum over positive ordinates up to \(e^{u/2}\); \(J\) bounds it above \(H\). Use \(1.83<\log(2\pi)<1.84, \log H>28.72\). Conjugate zeros double the weight; the reflected zeros left of the line cost at most the line contribution. Off-line zeros on the right above height \(H\) consume at most half the reciprocal sum above \(H\) by reflection. Writing their excess via the mesh gives
\[
 |\psi(e^u)/e^u-1| \le b_\beta(u)
 = U+ (J-C_0)_+e^{-(1-s_0)u}+Z_\beta(u).
 \tag{B}
\]
Only the two caps are compared here. In particular both yield a decaying error with the corresponding power and no positive log factor. We also have all original applicable envelopes and, under \(B_1\), the direct \(u^2e^{-5u/32}/64\) at \(u\ge200\). For \(\theta\), add the prime-power relative bound
\[
 D_+(u)=1.000000147e^{-u/2}+1.78e^{-2u/3}
\]
from Dusart 4.5, and intersect with all direct \(\theta\) bounds. One may use the tighter signed interval \([-b-D_+, b-D_-]\), with \(0\le D_-\le(\psi-\theta)/x\) as in §5. These transformations never decrease the established domains. Below 60 no explicit-formula claim is made by (B).

N=38358837682
m=isqrt(N)+1
s=bytearray(b'\1')*(m+1);s[:2]=b'\0\0'
for p in range(2,isqrt(m)+1):
 if s[p]:s[p*p:m+1:p]=b'\0'*((m-p*p)//p+1)
ps=[p for p in range(m+1) if s[p]]
M=2*3*5*7*11*13
w=[0]
for i in range(1,M+1):
 w.append(w[-1]+int(all(i%p for p in ps[:6])))
def cube(n):
 lo,hi=0,1
 while hi**3<=n:hi*=2
 while hi-lo>1:
  a=(hi+lo)//2
  if a**3<=n:lo=a
  else:hi=a

@lru_cache(maxsize=200000)
def phi(x,a):
 if a==0:return x
 if not x:return 0
 if a==6:return (x//M)*w[M]+w[x%M]
 if x<ps[a-1]:return 1
 if x<=m and x<ps[a]**2:return max(0,bisect_right(ps,x)-a)+1
 return phi(x,a-1)-phi(x//ps[a-1],a-1)
@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def P(x):
 if x<=m:return bisect_right(ps,x)
 a,b,c=map(P,(isqrt(isqrt(x)),isqrt(x),cube(x)))
 t=phi(x,a)+a-1
 for i in range(a,b):
  y=x//ps[i]
  t-=P(y)-i
  if i<c:
   for j in range(i,P(isqrt(y))):t-=P(y//ps[j])-j
 return t

Let \(n=38358837682\). Exact outputs from `endpoint.py`:
\[
 \pi(n)=\pi(n+1)=1644673232,\qquad
 \lfloor x/e\rfloor=14111427770,\quad \pi(x/e)=632207037
 \quad(n\le x\le n+1).
\]
The computation uses an ordinary Eratosthenes sieve up to \(\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor+1\), inclusion–exclusion \(\varphi(x,a)=\varphi(x,a-1)-\varphi(\lfloor x/p_{a-1}\rfloor,a-1)\) for the integers surviving the first \(a\) primes (0-based indices), plus a wheel for the first six primes. For \(a=\pi(x^{1/4})\), survivors aside from 1 and primes are products of two or three primes with indices at least \(a\), sorted with repetition allowed. Counting quadruples is unnecessary because their least possible product exceeds \(x\). For pairs, fix \(i\) up to \(p_i^2\le x\), count \(\pi(x/p_i)-i\); for triples fix \(i\) up to \(p_i^3\le x\) and \(j\ge i\) up to \(p_j^2\le x/p_i\), count \(\pi(x/(p_ip_j))-j\). Subtract these from \(\varphi+a-1\). All recursive arguments are smaller, with exact integer roots/divisions. The short base case of \(\varphi\) counts only 1 and surviving primes when the next surviving prime squared exceeds \(x\).

Thus \(r\) is the unique solution in this unit interval of \(e r(632207037)/\log r=(1644673232)^2\); monotonicity of \(t/\log t\) for \(t>e\) and the two certified signs give the bracket. In fact \(R(n)\) is about (-14736927.9) with a strictly negative interval. Consequently the literal real reading of PT 2021 Theorem 2 starting at \(x>n\) cannot hold. We do not use that reading as a premise.

def high(t,idx,n):
 # n is the last order kept, i.e. P_n contains 1 through L^{-n}.
 # Include n+1 as positive cushion; truncate pi at m=n+6.
 m=n+6;b=2*m+4;k=n+1
 assert t-1>=max(2*b,120,8*(k+7))
 u=I(t); v=u-1
 aa=[factorial(j) for j in range(m+1)]
 bb=[sum(aa[j]*aa[i-j] for j in range(m+1) if 0<=i-j<=m) for i in range(2*m+1)]
 def ap(u): return sum((a/u**i for i,a in enumerate(aa)),I(0))
 def rr(u):
  return factorial(m+1)*(u*E(u,Q(1,2))/b**(m+2)+
          1/(u**(m+1)*(1-2*(m+2)/u)))
 kap=2*I(b).exp()
 err=tail_pi_end(u,idx)+kap*u*E(u,1)+rr(u)
 erl=tail_pi_end(v,idx)+kap*v*E(v,1)
 loss=(u**4*(err*(2*ap(u)+err)+u/v*erl)+
       sum((bb[j]/u**(j-4) for j in range(m+1,2*m+1)),I(0)))*u**k
 lead=sum(aa[j]*comb(n+5,j) for j in range(n+6))-bb[n+5]
 return (I(lead)-loss).a
if __name__=='__main__':
 for n in [8,9,10,12,15,20]:
  for idx in [0,1]:
   a,b=250,1000; assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   while a+1<b:
    c=(a+b)//2
    if high(c,idx,n)>0:b=c
    else:a=c
   assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   print(n,idx,b,high(b,idx,n))

Define \(I_2(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t\). The normalization is deliberate. Partial summation gives
\[
 \pi(x)-I_2(x)=\frac{\theta(x)-x}{L}
   +\int_2^x\frac{\theta(t)-t}{t\log^2t}\,dt+\frac{2}{\log 2}.
\]
If \(B_\theta(u)\) is a bound for \(|\theta(e^u)/e^u-1|\), the dimensionless error for \(\pi/(x/L)\) is bounded by
\[
 b_\pi(L)=B_\theta(L)+Le^{-L}\left[2/\log2+
                 \int_{\log2}^L e^u B_\theta(u)\,du/u^2\right].
\]
The proof uses the minimum of relevant enclosures. Details of the enclosure used in `verify.py` follow, so no quadrature assumption is needed.

* CH2 Corollary 1.3 gives \(c+113.67e^{-u/2}\) for \(\psi\), with \(c=1.0472\cdot10^{-12}\); thus \(c+117e^{-u/2}\) bounds \(\theta\) for (u\ge\log 2). A second branch for \(u\ge34\) uses CH2 Corollary 1.2 at \(T=\min(e^{u/2}/2,3000175332800)\): if \(v=\log(T/(2\pi))\), its \(\psi\) radius is \(\pi/(T-1)+\pi^2/(3T^2)+(v^2/(2\pi)-v/(6\pi))e^{-u/2}\). Here \(x>\max(T,10^9),T\ge10^7\), and \(1/y\le\coth y\le1/y+y/3\) as in CH2 \(9.2\). Add \(D_+\).
* FiniteRH Corollary 1 gives \(.04u^2e^{-u/2}\) on \(6.4<u\le58.33\) \((e^{6.4}>599, e^{58.33}<2.169\cdot10^{25})\). For a prefix ending at \(e^v\) in this range the integral and normalizing constant together cost at most \(.08L e^{v/2-L}+1255Le^{-L}\). Use \(|\theta(t)-t|\le t\) for \(2\le t\le599\) (Dusart 4.2), and then the finite RH estimate itself on \(599<t\le e^v\). In particular the first line of `early` is this with \(v=L\).
* For a general prefix ending at \(e^v\), use \(c+117e^{-u/2}\). Split at \(u=v/2\) and use
\[
 \int_{\log2}^{v} e^{ku}du/u^2
 \le 4e^{kv}/(kv^2)+1.45e^{kv/2},\qquad k=1,1/2
\]
on the domains used. Multiply by \(Le^{-L}\) and add \(3Le^{-L}\) for the normalization.
* In the last 8 log units (if the finite RH branch holds throughout at the top) or last 16 units otherwise, divide into unit cells \(u=L-z, z\in[j,j+1]\). Multiply the interval bound for \(B_\theta(L-z)\) by \(L(e^{-j}-e^{-j-1})/(L-j-1)^2\). Use the minimum of the global, finite-height, (B), and direct-D02 radii that hold on that **whole** cell. For the upper \(\pi\) error only, if \(L\le39.47\), use also \(3Le^{-L}\) by \(\theta(t)<t\) (including \(\theta(2)\le2\)), since \(e^{39.47}<1.39\cdot10^{17}\). The lower error is not replaced by this one-sided bound.
* Analytic tail: for \(u\ge60\) majorize \(B_\theta(u)\) by
\[
 b^*(u)=(.04u^2+13u+2)e^{-u/2}+D_+(u)+.02u^2 e^{-.255u}+Z_\beta(u).
\]
Here \(U\) and \(J\) have the asserted polynomial majors by expansion. For \(L\ge120\), use this for the integral with \(u\ge L/2\), the general prefix up to \(v=L/2\), and the same \(b^*\) for the endpoint. For any term \(c u^j e^{-du}\), \(0<d\le2/3, j\ge0\), the late integral costs at most \((12/L)c L^j e^{-dL}\), since \(u^j\le L^j, u^{-2}\le4/L^2\) and \(\int_0^\infty e^{-(1-d)z}dz\le3\). \[

 assert t-1>=max(2*b,120,8*(k+7))
 u=I(t); v=u-1

def high(t,idx,n):
 # n is the last order kept, i.e. P_n contains 1 through L^{-n}.
 # Include n+1 as positive cushion; truncate pi at m=n+6.
 m=n+6;b=2*m+4;k=n+1
 assert t-1>=max(2*b,120,8*(k+7))
 u=I(t); v=u-1
 aa=[factorial(j) for j in range(m+1)]
 bb=[sum(aa[j]*aa[i-j] for j in range(m+1) if 0<=i-j<=m) for i in range(2*m+1)]
 def ap(u): return sum((a/u**i for i,a in enumerate(aa)),I(0))
 def rr(u):
  return factorial(m+1)*(u*E(u,Q(1,2))/b**(m+2)+
          1/(u**(m+1)*(1-2*(m+2)/u)))
 kap=2*I(b).exp()
 err=tail_pi_end(u,idx)+kap*u*E(u,1)+rr(u)
 erl=tail_pi_end(v,idx)+kap*v*E(v,1)
 loss=(u**4*(err*(2*ap(u)+err)+u/v*erl)+
       sum((bb[j]/u**(j-4) for j in range(m+1,2*m+1)),I(0)))*u**k
 lead=sum(aa[j]*comb(n+5,j) for j in range(n+6))-bb[n+5]
 return (I(lead)-loss).a
if __name__=='__main__':
 for n in [8,9,10,12,15,20]:
  for idx in [0,1]:
   a,b=250,1000; assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   while a+1<b:
    c=(a+b)//2
    if high(c,idx,n)>0:b=c
    else:a=c
   assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   print(n,idx,b,high(b,idx,n))

scopes.exact_span:
Set \(\mathcal P=e^\gamma L P_{\rm raw}\), \(\mathcal Q=e^{-\gamma}Q_{\rm raw}/L\),
\[
 E_1=\sum_{p\le x}1/p-\log L-M,\qquad
 E_w=\sum_{p\le x}\log(p)/p-L+B_3.
\]
The exact constants are \(M=\gamma+\sum_p(\log(1-1/p)+1/p)\) and \(B_3=\gamma+\sum_p\log p/[p(p-1)]\) (Dusart Theorems 5.6–5.7). For each row with exponent \(a\), all of \(|\mathcal P-1|,|\mathcal Q-1|,|E_1|\) are **at most** \(C x^{-a}/L\), and \(|E_w|\) is **at most** \(C x^{-a}\), on \(L\ge L_0\).

## 5. Forward kernels, signed spectrum, and smaller product errors

Use \(u=\log t\) in log-coordinate integrals. Set \(F(u)=\psi(e^u)e^{-u}-1\),
\[
 F_0(L)=\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n\log n}-\log L-\gamma,\qquad
 F_1(L)=\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n-L+\gamma,
\]
where the first sum starts at \(n=2\). To avoid index ambiguity, denote by \(W_j\) the centered weighted error with **weight \(t^{-1}(\log t)^{-j}\)**: \(W_0=F_1, W_1=F_0\). Partial summation with the boundary included yields
\[
 W_j(L)=L^{-j}F(L)-\int_L^\infty k_j(u)F(u)du,\quad
 k_j(u)=u^{-j}(1+j/u),\quad j=0,1. \tag{K}
\]
The centering constants follow from Dusart 5.6–5.7 and adding the absolutely convergent prime-power contributions. The limits and the integrals also follow from (B). Formula (K) holds for real \(x>1\); whether \(x\) is a prime power matters in the endpoint term, not a measure-zero change in the ordinary integral. Another exact identity is \(F_0(L)=F_1(L)/L-\int_L^\infty F_1(u)du/u^2\), by partial summation of the centered \(n^{-1}\Lambda(n)\) sum. The CH2 weighted bounds can therefore be used without the loss of integrating a constant relative error in \(\psi\) over the whole tail.

### Signed split

With the same \(T,T^\star\) as §2,
\[
 F(u)=-\sum_{\Re\rho\ge.745}\frac{e^{(\rho-1)u}}{\rho}+E(u),\qquad
 |E(u)|\le\sum_\nu b_\nu u^{n_\nu}e^{-d_\nu u}=:\mathcal R_a(u).
\]
Here the zero series includes both signs of the ordinate. Take the terms
\[
 (.04u^2+13u+2)e^{-u/2}+.02u^2e^{-.255u}
 +130(u/2)^4 e^{-(a+.16)u}+60((u/2)^2+u+2)e^{-(a+.5)u}.
\]
Indeed the low zeros and the Perron remainder are bounded by \(U+Je^{-.255u}\). For the high zeros omitted beyond \(T^\star\), integrate the density at \(s=.745\) from (T), using \(p=.68, d=.32, q=3.51, \log T=u/2-\log 6>28\). The log-power integral is at most \((\log T)^q T^{-d}/[d-q/\log T]\), since \((1+w/v)^q\le e^{qw/v}\). Here \(d-q/\log T>.19, 6^{.32}<2\) and \(c=6.1727\) (\(2\cdot6.1727\cdot2/.19<130\)); the second coefficient uses (2\cdot5\cdot6). The factor \(e^{-au}\) accounts for the real-part cap. With only Dusart's density replace 130, 60 by 220, 618; \(4.9\,3^{.68}<10.4\). The proof has no discontinuity issue because FKS 3.2 is for all real \(x\).

Termwise integration in (K) is justified by the convergent absolute reciprocal bound and the integrable majorant. For a high zero, integration by parts gives a bound \(2 k_j(L)e^{-(1-\Re\rho)L}/|\rho-1|\) on its integral before the \(1/\rho\) factor. Indeed \(k_j\) is positive nonincreasing, and \(\int_L^\infty|k_j'|\le k_j(L)\). As \(|\rho-1|\ge H\), the integrated error is tiny relative to the endpoint spectral term, rather than costing an extra factor of order \(1/a\). Consequently
\[
 L^j|W_j(L)|\le
 \left(1+\frac{2(1+j/L)}{H}\right)Z_\beta(L)

### Signed split

With the same \(T,T^\star\) as §2,
\[
 F(u)=-\sum_{\Re\rho\ge.745}\frac{e^{(\rho-1)u}}{\rho}+E(u),\qquad
 |E(u)|\le\sum_\nu b_\nu u^{n_\nu}e^{-d_\nu u}=:\mathcal R_a(u).
\]
Here the zero series includes both signs of the ordinate. Take the terms
\[
 (.04u^2+13u+2)e^{-u/2}+.02u^2e^{-.255u}
 +130(u/2)^4 e^{-(a+.16)u}+60((u/2)^2+u+2)e^{-(a+.5)u}.
\]
Indeed the low zeros and the Perron remainder are bounded by \(U+Je^{-.255u}\). For the high zeros omitted beyond \(T^\star\), integrate the density at \(s=.745\) from (T), using \(p=.68, d=.32, q=3.51, \log T=u/2-\log 6>28\). The log-power integral is at most \((\log T)^q T^{-d}/[d-q/\log T]\), since \((1+w/v)^q\le e^{qw/v}\). Here \(d-q/\log T>.19, 6^{.32}<2\) and \(c=6.1727\) (\(2\cdot6.1727\cdot2/.19<130\)); the second coefficient uses (2\cdot5\cdot6). The factor \(e^{-au}\) accounts for the real-part cap. With only Dusart's density replace 130, 60 by 220, 618; \(4.9\,3^{.68}<10.4\). The proof has no discontinuity issue because FKS 3.2 is for all real \(x\).

Termwise integration in (K) is justified by the convergent absolute reciprocal bound and the integrable majorant. For a high zero, integration by parts gives a bound \(2 k_j(L)e^{-(1-\Re\rho)L}/|\rho-1|\) on its integral before the \(1/\rho\) factor. scopes.exact_span:
Write \(D(t)=\psi(t)-\theta(t)\). The full omitted prime-power tail for weight \(t^{-1}(\log t)^{-j}\) is \(T_j(x)=\int_{(x,\infty)}t^{-1}(\log t)^{-j}dD(t)\). By positivity and parts,
\[
 0\le L^j T_j(x)\le 2.000000294e^{-L/2}+2.67e^{-2L/3}-D_-(L),
 \tag{T}
\]
where \(D_-=0\) is always allowed and for \(x\ge4\) we may use \(D_-=(1-\min(2.4646/L,15.86/L^2,166.64/L^3,2420.8/L^4))_+e^{-L/2}\). The lower bound on \(D(x)/x\) uses \(\theta\(\sqrt x\)\) and Dusart 4.2, with all four rows valid from \(\sqrt x=2\). For the integral upper, \(\int_L^\infty e^{-du}(u^{-j}+j u^{-j-1})dule e^{-dL}/(dL^j)\) for \(0<d<1\), by differentiating \(e^{-du}u^{-j}\); the endpoint term subtracts \(D(x)/(xL^j)\). This improves the crude integer prime-power estimates, including before spectral dominance.

Then \(E_w=W_0+T_0\), \(E_1=W_1+T_1\), and \(q=\log\mathcal Q=W_1+T_{1,\mathrm{tr}}\), the latter tail restricted to \(p\le x\) but \(p^k>x,k\ge2\). In particular \(0\le T_{1,\mathrm{tr}}\le T_1\). Equivalently \(q=E_1-A_{>x}\) with \(0\le A_{>x}=\sum_{p>x,k\ge2}1/(kp^k)\le1/(2\lfloor x\rfloor)\) by comparison to half the telescoping sum \(1/[n(n-1)]\). These are exact, with the claimed normalizers, not first-order approximations. A symmetric bound \(r\) for (|q|) yields \(\max(|\mathcal P-1|,|\mathcal Q-1|)\le e^r-1\le r e^r\). For a second branch, define
\[
 C_R^*(s)=2\left[\frac{4.9\,3^p h^q e^{-dh}}{d-q/h}
      +51.5\frac{h^2+2h+2}{H}\right].
\]
It is an upper bound for the cumulative reciprocal count by the same log-power integral bound. Its logarithmic derivative is no more than 105 in absolute value on \([.745,7/8]\): for the nonconstant term bound it by \(2\log h+(8/3)(h+\log 3)+(8/3+2/h)/(.32-3.51/h)<105\), and the additive constant has derivative zero. Integrating the cumulative bound by parts in the *real part*, not the ordinate, thus gives for \(L>105\)
\[
 \sum_{\Re\rho\ge.745} |e^{(\rho-1)L}/\rho|
 \le C_R^*(\beta)e^{-aL}\frac{L}{L-105}.
 \tag{C}
\]
In detail the scaled bound is \(C_R^*(.745)e^{-(\beta-.745)L}+L\int_{.745}^\beta C_R^*(s)e^{-(\beta-s)L}ds\); bound \(C_R^*(s)\) by \(C_R^*(\beta)e^{105(\beta-s)}\), then add. Replace \(Z_\beta\) in (M) by the minimum of (Z) and (C). This gives the further rows with \(L_0\ge600\), again by monotonic normalized comparison (\(L/(L-105)\) decreases). It gives limiting upper coefficients \(C_R^*(7/8)<.006740\), \(C_R^*(27/32)<.118072\); the non-spectral terms vanish relative to the target. For the sharper signed-series limsup bound \(\limsup\le C(\beta)\), and its refinement at the full height, see the exact-kernel calculation in repair.md §2. In particular one cannot simply replace the finite multiplier in (M) by 1 at the limit. No boundary zero is asserted.

def rp(J,u):

 # theta(sqrt(x)) >= sqrt(x)*(1-2*1.2323/L), for sqrt(x)>=2.

 # list (constant, monomial degree, rate)
 m,n=(220,618) if RAM_ONLY else (130,60)
 return [(I('.04'),2,Q(1,2)),(I(13),1,Q(1,2)),(I(2),0,Q(1,2)),

 return (1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H)*z+sum((c*u**n*E(u,d)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))

def rp(J,u):
 # scaled prime-power tail (full), relative constants from Dusart Cor 4.5, Thm 4.2.
 v=(I('1.000000147')*2*E(u,Q(1,2))+I('1.78')*I('1.5')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
 # theta(sqrt(x)) >= sqrt(x)*(1-2*1.2323/L), for sqrt(x)>=2.
 return v-pp_lower(u)
def rparts(a):
 # list (constant, monomial degree, rate)
 m,n=(220,618) if RAM_ONLY else (130,60)
 return [(I('.04'),2,Q(1,2)),(I(13),1,Q(1,2)),(I(2),0,Q(1,2)),
         (I('.02'),2,Q(255,1000)),(I(m)/16,4,a+Q(16,100)),
         (I(n)/4,2,a+Q(1,2)),(I(n),1,a+Q(1,2)),(I(2*n),0,a+Q(1,2))]
def sig(lo,hi,idx,j):
 # Upper bound for scaled error L^j times |F_j| (before prime powers).
 u=I(lo,hi);a=1-BETA[idx]
 z=zp(lo,hi,idx,mode='zeros')
 return (1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H)*z+sum((c*u**n*E(u,d)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
def pure(t,idx,j,theta=True):
 # bound on e^(a*L) L^j times |log error or sum error| for all L>=t
 u=I(t);a=1-BETA[idx]
 g,w,w0=grid(BETA[idx],745)
 z=sum((c*E(u,1-s-a) for s,c in zip(g[1:],w)),I(0))
 ans=(1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H)*z
 ans+=sum((c*u**n*E(u,d-a)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
 for c,n,d in rparts(a):assert t*(d-a)>n
 if theta:ans+=(I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q(1,2)-a)+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)-a))*(1+I(j)/u)
 return ans
def wc(lo,hi,j):
 u=I(lo,hi)
 c=I('1.0472e-12');f=I('3.142e-7');t=I('27.6')
 ch1=mn(ch(u),f+33*E(u,Q(1,2)))
 ch0=(mn(2*c+I('113.67')*E(u,Q(1,2))*(1+2/u),
         2*f+33*E(u,Q(1,2))*(1+2/u)))
 if hi<=D('27.6'):
  pre=I('.8')*E(u,Q(1,2))
  if not j:return pre
  tail=mn(c/t+I('227.34')*E(t,Q(1,2))/t**2,
          f/t+66*E(t,Q(1,2))/t**2)
  return pre*(1+2/u)+u*tail
 return ch0 if j else ch1
def origpoly(lo,hi,j):

 guards(169)

def polycheck():
 from certify import cutoff
 assert I('17.95').exp().a>121
 for t,j,c in [('18.05',1,'.08'),('18.15',1,'.077'),('20',1,'.037'),
               ('17.95',0,'.079'),('18',0,'.0774'),('20',0,'.035')]:
  def check(lo,hi):
   u=I(lo,hi)
   z=wc(lo,hi,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3))
   if lo>=60:z=mn(z,sig(lo,hi,0,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
   return (I(c)-u*u*z*( (z/u).exp() if j else 1)).a
  b=200;a=D(t);k=D('27.6')

 return 2*(I('4.9')*ex(f(p)*I(3).ln()+f(q)*h.ln()-f(d)*h)/(f(d)-f(q)/h)

def pp_lower(u):
 return pos(1-mn(I('2.4646')/u,I('15.86')/u**2,I('166.64')/u**3,I('2420.8')/u**4))*E(u,Q(1,2))
def rp(J,u):
 # scaled prime-power tail (full), relative constants from Dusart Cor 4.5, Thm 4.2.
 v=(I('1.000000147')*2*E(u,Q(1,2))+I('1.78')*I('1.5')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
 # theta(sqrt(x)) >= sqrt(x)*(1-2*1.2323/L), for sqrt(x)>=2.
 return v-pp_lower(u)
def rparts(a):
 # list (constant, monomial degree, rate)
 m,n=(220,618) if RAM_ONLY else (130,60)
 return [(I('.04'),2,Q(1,2)),(I(13),1,Q(1,2)),(I(2),0,Q(1,2)),
         (I('.02'),2,Q(255,1000)),(I(m)/16,4,a+Q(16,100)),
         (I(n)/4,2,a+Q(1,2)),(I(n),1,a+Q(1,2)),(I(2*n),0,a+Q(1,2))]
def sig(lo,hi,idx,j):
 # Upper bound for scaled error L^j times |F_j| (before prime powers).
 u=I(lo,hi);a=1-BETA[idx]
 z=zp(lo,hi,idx,mode='zeros')
 return (1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H)*z+sum((c*u**n*E(u,d)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
def pure(t,idx,j,theta=True):
 # bound on e^(a*L) L^j times |log error or sum error| for all L>=t
 u=I(t);a=1-BETA[idx]
 g,w,w0=grid(BETA[idx],745)
 z=sum((c*E(u,1-s-a) for s,c in zip(g[1:],w)),I(0))
 ans=(1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H)*z
 ans+=sum((c*u**n*E(u,d-a)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
 for c,n,d in rparts(a):assert t*(d-a)>n
 if theta:ans+=(I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q(1,2)-a)+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)-a))*(1+I(j)/u)
 return ans
def wc(lo,hi,j):
 u=I(lo,hi)
 c=I('1.0472e-12');f=I('3.142e-7');t=I('27.6')
 ch1=mn(ch(u),f+33*E(u,Q(1,2)))
 ch0=(mn(2*c+I('113.67')*E(u,Q(1,2))*(1+2/u),
         2*f+33*E(u,Q(1,2))*(1+2/u)))
 if hi<=D('27.6'):
  pre=I('.8')*E(u,Q(1,2))
  if not j:return pre
  tail=mn(c/t+I('227.34')*E(t,Q(1,2))/t**2,
          f/t+66*E(t,Q(1,2))/t**2)
  return pre*(1+2/u)+u*tail
 return ch0 if j else ch1
def origpoly(lo,hi,j):
 # An entire-cell bound for L^(2+j) times the error.
 u=I(lo,hi)
 z=wc(lo,hi,j)+rp(j,u)
 if lo>=60:z=mn(z,sig(lo,hi,0,j)+rp(j,u))
 return z*u*u, z/u**j

\]
The factor changing this sum to the first weighted prime-power tail is at most \(1+1/N\); use the wider interval \([.997,1.004]/N\).
* For the other tail, \(\sum_{p>N}1/(2p^2)\) is within
\(\delta(3+1/u)/(2Nu)\) of \(\int_N^\infty dt/(2t^2\log t)\), by parts with weight \(1/(2t^2\log t)\). By integrating by parts once, this integral is between \((1-1/u)/(2Nu)\) and \(1/(2Nu)\). The remaining powers multiply the upper by at most \(1+2/N\) (sum a geometric series). With the log bracket this gives \([1.38,1.50]\cdot10^{-9}\). All threshold numerical conditions follow by elementary integer calculations and the log enclosure above, or by the verified Decimal checks.

Combine with \(\gamma\) to enclose \(M\) and \(B_3\) at common denominator Q. The program prints the endpoints, and they can also be used to give pointwise enclosures for any finite prime-sum calculation. No table of tabulated values of the constants is assumed.

scopes.exact_span: * **Source Chebyshev minima.** For \(\psi\), take the applicable minima of FiniteRH Cor. 1, CH2 Cor. 1.2 for any admissible \(10^7\le T\le3000175332800\), Cor. 1.3, Lemma 9.2, \(10.3\), Dusart Thm. 3.3 and Table 1, FKS Cor. 1.4, Lemma 5.2 **restricted to \( .85\le L\le2100 \)** as proved in `repair.md`, and step values in its proof, Thms. 1.1–1.2 (in particular all applicable rows of Tables 5–6), and PT 2021 Thm. 1 (both radii from each row). Rows at a threshold inconsistent with the theorem's strict premise are not needed (\(L_0=1000\) in FKS 1.1–1.2); use its repaired Lemma 5.2 instead on that range. For \(1<x<2\), use the exact relative Chebyshev error \(-1\) when needed. `source-tables.json` records the tabulated arguments; a displayed rounded analytic value can safely be enlarged by \(1.001\) if needed for an outward table interpretation. For \(\theta\) include direct Dusart 4.2, FiniteRH Cor. 1, PT Cor. 1 and \(18\), and all transfers from \(\psi\) with the indicated prime-power correction. This is a portfolio minimum, not a claim of optimal tuning over all possible proofs.

def C_r(s):
 p=Q(8,3)*(1-s);q=5-2*s;d=1-p
 return 2*(I('4.9')*ex(f(p)*I(3).ln()+f(q)*h.ln()-f(d)*h)/(f(d)-f(q)/h)
          +I('51.5')*(h*h+2*h+2)/H)
def cont(u,idx,j):
 # Scaled by exp(aL); no prime-power subtraction needed.
 u=I(u);a=1-BETA[idx]
 z=C_r(BETA[idx])*u/(u-105)
 z*=1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H
 z+=sum((c*u**n*E(u,d-a)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
 z+=(I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q(1,2)-a)+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)-a))*(1+I(j)/u)
 return z

  assert (I(val).ln()+I(max(L,L0))/8-base).a>0,(L,val)

  L=max(L,L0);x=I(L)/I(R)

  assert (I(A).ln()+I(B)*x.ln()-I(Cc)*sqrt(x)+I(L)/8-base).a>0

scopes.exact_span:
For clarity, here is an entire-domain prescription, including ranges where a convenient power row is not smallest. In all branches only apply a source formula within its domain. The direct polynomial bounds of Dusart 5.6–5.9 and independently joined rows above are always retained. At very small \(x\) the prime sums or products themselves are finite and can alternatively be evaluated with the constant intervals in `finite-evidence.txt`; for \(1<x<2\) the prime sums are empty and the raw products are one.

* **Source Chebyshev minima.** For \(\psi\), take the applicable minima of FiniteRH Cor. 1, CH2 Cor. 1.2 for any admissible \(10^7\le T\le3000175332800\), Cor. 1.3, Lemma 9.2, \(10.3\), Dusart Thm. 3.3 and Table 1, FKS Cor. 1.4, Lemma 5.2 **restricted to \( .85\le L\le2100 \)** as proved in `repair.md`, and step values in its proof, Thms. 1.1–1.2 (in particular all applicable rows of Tables 5–6), and PT 2021 Thm. 1 (both radii from each row). Rows at a threshold inconsistent with the theorem's strict premise are not needed (\(L_0=1000\) in FKS 1.1–1.2); use its repaired Lemma 5.2 instead on that range. For \(1<x<2\), use the exact relative Chebyshev error \(-1\) when needed. `source-tables.json` records the tabulated arguments; a displayed rounded analytic value can safely be enlarged by \(1.001\) if needed for an outward table interpretation. For \(\theta\) include direct Dusart 4.2, FiniteRH Cor. 1, PT Cor. 1 and \(18\), and all transfers from \(\psi\) with the indicated prime-power correction. This is a portfolio minimum, not a claim of optimal tuning over all possible proofs.
* **Kernel minima.** In both treatments include (B) with the respective cap and all \(B_0\) branches. Include the signed boxes from (M) and (T), the continuous alternative (C), and the direct D02 \(\psi\) majorant only at its allowed threshold. If \(b(u)\) is a pointwise envelope for the absolute error in relative \(\psi\) or \(\theta\), the transformed weighted radius is \(b(L)L^{-j}+\int_L^\infty k_j(u)b(u)du\). For \(\psi\) this bounds \(W_j\), for \(\theta\) it directly bounds \(E_w\) \((j=0)\) or \(E_1\) \((j=1)\), by Dusart's identities (or partial summation). Intersect **before and after** integral transfer: take the minimum under the integral, as well as any independently smaller output bounds that are not unsigned transfers. For signed relative boxes \([l(u),v(u)]\), use endpoint lower minus integral of upper and endpoint upper minus integral of lower. The minimum functions are measurable (the tabulated branches are piecewise continuous; for a continuum of CH2 parameters it suffices to take a countable dense set and its one-sided endpoint limits). Integrate the cumulative envelopes which include an integrable branch from (B), or FKS 1.4 independently. For the unsigned reverse transfer from \(E_1\) to \(q\) use \([-r-A_{>x},r]\), and for a \(W_1\) radius use \([-r,r+T_1]\), then intersect and exponentiate as above. Similarly the signed \(W_0\) weighted tail box is \([-r,r+T_0]\). The separate direct CH2 bound on \(F_1\) and its transfer to \(F_0\) augment these, not substitute for them. The direct D02 unsigned kernel without the density argument, for example, gives
\[
 |W_0|\le e^{-aL}(L^2+L^2/a+2L/a^2+2/a^3)/64,\quad
 |W_1|\le e^{-aL}(L+(L+1)/a+1/a^2)/64,\quad a=5/32,\quad L\ge200 .
\]
The signed spectral table improves these by orders of magnitude (even the normalized endpoint cost of the direct input alone is \(L^2/64\ge625\) versus .226). The important advance is reducing the exponent by \(1/32\) **relative to the QRH-aware comparator**, not just beating the original inverse logarithms.

def C_r(s):
 p=Q(8,3)*(1-s);q=5-2*s;d=1-p
 return 2*(I('4.9')*ex(f(p)*I(3).ln()+f(q)*h.ln()-f(d)*h)/(f(d)-f(q)/h)
          +I('51.5')*(h*h+2*h+2)/H)
def cont(u,idx,j):

 return z

scopes.exact_span: * **Whole-domain comparison.** The \(B_1\) envelope includes the \(B_0\) envelope identically, so no joins can make it worse, on their entire domains. Strict improvement for \(L\ge200\) can be proved against the enumerated finite original-output and transfer branches, not inferred from samples: every explicit original tabulated \(\psi\) radius in `source-tables.json` and the indicated original polynomial/exponential branches is at least \(.005e^{-L/8}\) on that matched domain. For constants check the onset (or 200), for \(A L^be^{-c\sqrt L}\) check the onset and use \(1/8-c/(2\sqrt L)>0\) in the logarithmic ratio; for inverse powers use \(1/8-k/L>0\). CH2's admissible finite-height branch has floor \(>1.047\cdot10^{-12}\). The terminal mesh coefficient in (Z) for \(B_0\) exceeds .005 (check in `comparison.py`), and \(C_R^*(7/8)>.005\). Thus each of the \(B_0\) transfers here has an endpoint radius at least the guard (divided by (L) for the normalized log quantities). One-sided prime-power boxes also contain both signs of this guard: for the \(\theta\)-sourced product box use \(q=E_1-A_{>x}\), for the \(\psi\)-sourced one \(q=W_1+T_{1,\rm tr}\); the endpoint \(\theta\) correction \(D_-,D_+\) is \(o(e^{-L/8})\) and is less than \(.001e^{-L/8}\) throughout this ray. Even allowing that subtraction, or applying \(1-e^{-r}\ge r-r^2/2\), a conservative surviving matched scaled guard is \(.002e^{-L/8}\). The direct \(B_0\) product bounds can be intersected in log coordinates using their logarithms; they also contain this smaller guard. The inequality \(.226e^{-200/32}<.002\) proves the claimed strict ordering against these branches; the original inverse-logarithm radii are also dominated simply by the decreasing ratio \(CL^2e^{-aL}\) after the listed onsets. This strict ordering is not a lower bound for actual prime errors, nor an extremal statement about unenumerated choices of analytic estimates, such as a new optimization of the parameters in FKS \(4.1\). The retained minima permit those legal original choices as additional boxes; the strict comparison here is to the enumerated explicit branches.

def C_r(s):
 p=Q(8,3)*(1-s);q=5-2*s;d=1-p
 return 2*(I('4.9')*ex(f(p)*I(3).ln()+f(q)*h.ln()-f(d)*h)/(f(d)-f(q)/h)
          +I('51.5')*(h*h+2*h+2)/H)
def cont(u,idx,j):
 # Scaled by exp(aL); no prime-power subtraction needed.
 u=I(u);a=1-BETA[idx]
 z=C_r(BETA[idx])*u/(u-105)
 z*=1+2*(1+I(j)/u)/H
 z+=sum((c*u**n*E(u,d-a)*(1+(1+I(j)/u)/(f(d)-n/u)) for c,n,d in rparts(a)),I(0))
 z+=(I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q(1,2)-a)+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)-a))*(1+I(j)/u)
 return z
def guards(L0=200):
 # Check against 0.005 exp(-L/8) for relative endpoint radii.
 # For j=1 this is the normalized radius after multiplication by L.
 tab=json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name('source-tables.json').read_text())
 base=I('.005').ln()
 def check_const(L,val):
  assert (I(val).ln()+I(max(L,L0))/8-base).a>0,(L,val)
 def check_curve(L,A,B,Cc,R='1'):
  L=max(L,L0);x=I(L)/I(R)
  # The log derivative has lower bound 1/8 - C/(2 sqrt(R L)), so applies if B>=0.
  assert D(B)>=0 and (I(1)/8-I(Cc)/(2*sqrt(I(L)*I(R)))).a>0
  assert (I(A).ln()+I(B)*x.ln()-I(Cc)*sqrt(x)+I(L)/8-base).a>0
 def check_poly(L,coef,k):
  L=max(L,L0)
  assert L>8*k
  assert (I(coef).ln()-k*I(L).ln()+I(L)/8-base).a>0
 for name in ['FKS-5','Dusart-1']:
  for L,val in tab[name]:check_const(int(L),val)
 for L,v,b,c,k in tab['PT-1']:
  check_const(int(L),k);check_curve(int(L),v,b,c,'5.573412')
 # 0.848 > 2 / sqrt(5.5666305), safe test for FKS Table 6.
 assert (2/sqrt(I('5.5666305'))).b<D('.848')
 # Change the normalization from (L/R)^1.5 to L^1.5.
 for L,v in tab['FKS-6']:check_curve(int(L),str((I(v)/14).a),'1.5','.848')
 assert (I('5.5666305')*sqrt(I('5.5666305'))).b<14
 assert (I('5.573412')*sqrt(I('5.573412'))).b<14
 check_curve(L0,'9.22022','1.5','.8476836');check_curve(L0,'2','1.5','.8476836')
 check_curve(L0,'.18','.25','.394') # PT (18) fallback, weakened in both directions
 if L0>=200:check_const(200,'1.047e-12')
 check_const(1000,'1.94751e-12');check_const(40,'1.93378e-8')
 for c,k in [('.001',1),('.01',2),('.5',3),('34.409',4),('59.18',4),('151.3',4),('.035',2)]:check_poly(L0,c,k)
 assert grid(BETA[0],745)[1][-1].a>D('.005')
 assert (I('.004')-I('.226')*E(I(200),Q(1,32))).a>0
 assert (I('.0135')*E(I(224),Q(1,8))).b < D('1e-14')
 assert (I('.238')*E(I(198),Q(5,32))).b < D('1e-14')
 assert (I('.0111')*E(I(296),Q(1,8))).b < D('1e-18')
 assert (I('.193')*E(I(255),Q(5,32))).b < D('1e-18')
 print('row counts', {k:len(v) for k,v in tab.items()}, 'non-CH2 endpoint guard .005 from log',L0)
def continuous():
 assert (I('.32')-I('3.51')/h).a>D('.197')
 s=2*h.ln()+f(Q(8,3))*(h+I(3).ln())+(f(Q(8,3))+2/h)/(I('.32')-I('3.51')/h)
 assert s.b<105
 for i,rows in enumerate([{600:'.0082',1000:'.0076',2000:'.0072',4000:'.0070',10000:'.0069'},
                       {600:'.144',1000:'.132',2000:'.125',4000:'.122',10000:'.120'}]):
  print('boundary coefficient',i,C_r(BETA[i]),'Taylor bound',dens(BETA[i]))
  for L,val in rows.items():
   c=cont(L,i,1);d=cont(L,i,0)
   assert (I(val)-c*(c*E(I(L),1-BETA[i])/L).exp()).a>0 and (I(val)-d).a>0
   assert all((L*(rate-1+BETA[i]))>n for _,n,rate in rparts(1-BETA[i]))
   print('continuous',i,L,val,c.b,d.b)
 assert (I('.226')*E(I(200),Q(1,32))).b<D('.002')
 assert (I('.226')/I('.0135')*E(I(200),Q(1,32))).b<D('.033')
 assert (I('.025')*I(180)**2*E(I(180),Q(1,8))).b<D('.2')
 assert (I('.431')*I(160)**2*E(I(160),Q(5,32))).b<D('.2')
 assert (I('1.000000147')*E(I(200),Q(3,8))+I('1.78')*E(I(200),Q(13,24))).b<D('.001')
if __name__=='__main__':aux();guards();continuous()

def certify_refine():
 from certify import cutoff
 from comparison import guards
 aux()
 assert I(65).exp().a/6>HT
 assert (hh-I('28.72')).a>0
 # FKS Lemma 5.2 domain repair; on [.85,1] exactly one prime power is present.
 assert I('.85').exp().a>2 and I(1).exp().b<3
 assert (I('.8476836')**2*4).b<9
 def fks(u):
  return 2*powq(u,Q(3,2))*E(powq(u,Q(1,2)),Q('.8476836'))
 assert min(fks(I(1)).a,fks(I(40)).a)>D('.77')
 assert (I('.8476836')**2*40).a>9
 assert fks(I(1000)).a>D('1.93378e-8') and fks(I(2100)).a>D('1.94751e-12')
 print('FKS small-domain repair',cutoff('.85','1',lambda lo,hi:(fks(I(lo,hi))-1+I(2).ln()*E(I(lo,hi),1)).a))
 # Both the historical statements and the tighter refined rows are tested.
 for name,rows in [('restored',ORIG),('refined',NEW)]:
  for i,row in enumerate(rows):
   for t,v in row:
    z=common(t,i);assert z.b<D(v)
    print(name,i,t,v,z.b)
 for i,row in enumerate(CONT):
  for t,v in zip([600,1000,2000,4000,10000],row):
   z=common(t,i,start=7450,continuous=True);assert z.b<D(v)
   print('continuous',i,t,v,z.b)
 for i,t,v in [(0,'185.8','.01343'),(1,'167.75','.265')]:
  u=I(t);a=1-BETA[i];g=I(v)
  z=common(t,i);assert z.b<g.a
  b=I('113.67')*(1+2/I(50))+I('2.000000294')+I('2.67')
  zz=I('1.0472e-12')*E(u,-a)+g/(f(a)*u)+b*E(I(50),Q('.5')-a)
  assert (f(a)*u).a>1
  # Upper bound for unscaled j=1 radius for 50<=L<=t.
  logcap=(2*I('1.0472e-12')+g*E(u,a)/(f(a)*u)+b*E(I(50),Q('.5')))/50
  assert (zz*logcap.exp()).b<g.a,(i,t,v,zz)
  for lo,hi,c in [('13.7','20','.3'),('20','50','.04')]:
   assert max((I(c)*E(I(w),-a)/I(w)**2).b for w in (lo,hi))<g.a
  assert I('13.7').exp().b<912560
  print('connected',i,t,v,z.b,(zz*logcap.exp()).b)
 for i,t,v in [(0,223,'1e-14'),(1,197,'1e-14'),(0,295,'1e-18'),(1,255,'1e-18')]:
  z=common(t,i)*E(I(t),1-BETA[i]); assert z.b<D(v)
  print('target',i,t,v,z.b)
 guards(169)
 assert mesh(0,7200,5)[1][-1].a>D('.005')
 assert moment(Q(7,8),ram=True).a>D('.005')
 u=I(169); g=I('.263')
 assert common(169,1).b<g.a
 assert (g*E(u,Q(5,32))).b<D('.9')*D('1.047e-12')
 assert (g*E(u,Q(1,32))).b<D('.9')*D('.005')
 assert (u*E(u,Q(1,2))).b<1
 assert pp(u).b<D('.001')*D('1.047e-12')
 assert (pp(u)*E(u,-Q(1,8))).b<D('.001')*D('.005')
 assert (I('.221')/I('.01256')*E(I(200),Q(1,32))).b<D('.035')
 print('strict pointwise guard from log 169')
 polycheck()
 for i in range(2):print('Taylor cap',i,moment(BETA[i],ram=True))
def polycheck():
 from certify import cutoff
 assert I('17.95').exp().a>121
 for t,j,c in [('18.05',1,'.08'),('18.15',1,'.077'),('20',1,'.037'),
               ('17.95',0,'.079'),('18',0,'.0774'),('20',0,'.035')]:
  def check(lo,hi):
   u=I(lo,hi)
   z=wc(lo,hi,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3))
   if lo>=60:z=mn(z,sig(lo,hi,0,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
   return (I(c)-u*u*z*( (z/u).exp() if j else 1)).a
  b=200;a=D(t);k=D('27.6')
  p=cutoff(a,k,check);q=cutoff(k,b,check)
  u=I(200);z=(sig(D(200),D(200),0,j)+I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
  loss=z*u*u*((z/u).exp() if j else 1)
  assert loss.b<D(c)
  print('sharper polynomial',t,j,c,p,q,loss.b)
if __name__=='__main__':certify_refine()

def high(t,idx,n):
 # n is the last order kept, i.e. P_n contains 1 through L^{-n}.
 # Include n+1 as positive cushion; truncate pi at m=n+6.
 m=n+6;b=2*m+4;k=n+1
 assert t-1>=max(2*b,120,8*(k+7))
 u=I(t); v=u-1
 aa=[factorial(j) for j in range(m+1)]
 bb=[sum(aa[j]*aa[i-j] for j in range(m+1) if 0<=i-j<=m) for i in range(2*m+1)]
 def ap(u): return sum((a/u**i for i,a in enumerate(aa)),I(0))
 def rr(u):
  return factorial(m+1)*(u*E(u,Q(1,2))/b**(m+2)+
          1/(u**(m+1)*(1-2*(m+2)/u)))
 kap=2*I(b).exp()
 err=tail_pi_end(u,idx)+kap*u*E(u,1)+rr(u)
 erl=tail_pi_end(v,idx)+kap*v*E(v,1)
 loss=(u**4*(err*(2*ap(u)+err)+u/v*erl)+
       sum((bb[j]/u**(j-4) for j in range(m+1,2*m+1)),I(0)))*u**k
 lead=sum(aa[j]*comb(n+5,j) for j in range(n+6))-bb[n+5]
 return (I(lead)-loss).a
if __name__=='__main__':
 for n in [8,9,10,12,15,20]:
  for idx in [0,1]:
   a,b=250,1000; assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   while a+1<b:
    c=(a+b)//2
    if high(c,idx,n)>0:b=c
    else:a=c
   assert high(b,idx,n)>0
   print(n,idx,b,high(b,idx,n))

 bb=[sum(aa[j]*aa[i-j] for j in range(m+1) if 0<=i-j<=m) for i in range(2*m+1)]
 def ap(u): return sum((a/u**i for i,a in enumerate(aa)),I(0))

def high(t,idx,n):
 # n is the last order kept, i.e. P_n contains 1 through L^{-n}.
 # Include n+1 as positive cushion; truncate pi at m=n+6.
 m=n+6;b=2*m+4;k=n+1
 assert t-1>=max(2*b,120,8*(k+7))
 u=I(t); v=u-1
 aa=[factorial(j) for j in range(m+1)]
 bb=[sum(aa[j]*aa[i-j] for j in range(m+1) if 0<=i-j<=m) for i in range(2*m+1)]
 def ap(u): return sum((a/u**i for i,a in enumerate(aa)),I(0))
 def rr(u):
  return factorial(m+1)*(u*E(u,Q(1,2))/b**(m+2)+
          1/(u**(m+1)*(1-2*(m+2)/u)))
 kap=2*I(b).exp()
 err=tail_pi_end(u,idx)+kap*u*E(u,1)+rr(u)
 erl=tail_pi_end(v,idx)+kap*v*E(v,1)
 loss=(u**4*(err*(2*ap(u)+err)+u/v*erl)+
       sum((bb[j]/u**(j-4) for j in range(m+1,2*m+1)),I(0)))*u**k
 lead=sum(aa[j]*comb(n+5,j) for j in range(n+6))-bb[n+5]
 return (I(lead)-loss).a

 for n in [8,9,10,12,15,20]:

def certify_refine():
 from certify import cutoff
 from comparison import guards
 aux()
 assert I(65).exp().a/6>HT
 assert (hh-I('28.72')).a>0
 # FKS Lemma 5.2 domain repair; on [.85,1] exactly one prime power is present.
 assert I('.85').exp().a>2 and I(1).exp().b<3
 assert (I('.8476836')**2*4).b<9
 def fks(u):
  return 2*powq(u,Q(3,2))*E(powq(u,Q(1,2)),Q('.8476836'))
 assert min(fks(I(1)).a,fks(I(40)).a)>D('.77')
 assert (I('.8476836')**2*40).a>9
 assert fks(I(1000)).a>D('1.93378e-8') and fks(I(2100)).a>D('1.94751e-12')
 print('FKS small-domain repair',cutoff('.85','1',lambda lo,hi:(fks(I(lo,hi))-1+I(2).ln()*E(I(lo,hi),1)).a))
 # Both the historical statements and the tighter refined rows are tested.
 for name,rows in [('restored',ORIG),('refined',NEW)]:
  for i,row in enumerate(rows):
   for t,v in row:
    z=common(t,i);assert z.b<D(v)
    print(name,i,t,v,z.b)
 for i,row in enumerate(CONT):
  for t,v in zip([600,1000,2000,4000,10000],row):
   z=common(t,i,start=7450,continuous=True);assert z.b<D(v)
   print('continuous',i,t,v,z.b)
 for i,t,v in [(0,'185.8','.01343'),(1,'167.75','.265')]:
  u=I(t);a=1-BETA[i];g=I(v)
  z=common(t,i);assert z.b<g.a
  b=I('113.67')*(1+2/I(50))+I('2.000000294')+I('2.67')
  zz=I('1.0472e-12')*E(u,-a)+g/(f(a)*u)+b*E(I(50),Q('.5')-a)
  assert (f(a)*u).a>1
  # Upper bound for unscaled j=1 radius for 50<=L<=t.
  logcap=(2*I('1.0472e-12')+g*E(u,a)/(f(a)*u)+b*E(I(50),Q('.5')))/50
  assert (zz*logcap.exp()).b<g.a,(i,t,v,zz)
  for lo,hi,c in [('13.7','20','.3'),('20','50','.04')]:
   assert max((I(c)*E(I(w),-a)/I(w)**2).b for w in (lo,hi))<g.a
  assert I('13.7').exp().b<912560
  print('connected',i,t,v,z.b,(zz*logcap.exp()).b)
 for i,t,v in [(0,223,'1e-14'),(1,197,'1e-14'),(0,295,'1e-18'),(1,255,'1e-18')]:
  z=common(t,i)*E(I(t),1-BETA[i]); assert z.b<D(v)
  print('target',i,t,v,z.b)
 guards(169)
 assert mesh(0,7200,5)[1][-1].a>D('.005')
 assert moment(Q(7,8),ram=True).a>D('.005')
 u=I(169); g=I('.263')
 assert common(169,1).b<g.a
 assert (g*E(u,Q(5,32))).b<D('.9')*D('1.047e-12')
 assert (g*E(u,Q(1,32))).b<D('.9')*D('.005')
 assert (u*E(u,Q(1,2))).b<1
 assert pp(u).b<D('.001')*D('1.047e-12')
 assert (pp(u)*E(u,-Q(1,8))).b<D('.001')*D('.005')
 assert (I('.221')/I('.01256')*E(I(200),Q(1,32))).b<D('.035')
 print('strict pointwise guard from log 169')
 polycheck()
 for i in range(2):print('Taylor cap',i,moment(BETA[i],ram=True))
def polycheck():
 from certify import cutoff
 assert I('17.95').exp().a>121
 for t,j,c in [('18.05',1,'.08'),('18.15',1,'.077'),('20',1,'.037'),
               ('17.95',0,'.079'),('18',0,'.0774'),('20',0,'.035')]:
  def check(lo,hi):
   u=I(lo,hi)
   z=wc(lo,hi,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3))
   if lo>=60:z=mn(z,sig(lo,hi,0,j)+I('1.000100294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
   return (I(c)-u*u*z*( (z/u).exp() if j else 1)).a
  b=200;a=D(t);k=D('27.6')
  p=cutoff(a,k,check);q=cutoff(k,b,check)
  u=I(200);z=(sig(D(200),D(200),0,j)+I('2.000000294')*E(u,Q('.5'))+I('2.67')*E(u,Q(2,3)))
  loss=z*u*u*((z/u).exp() if j else 1)
  assert loss.b<D(c)
  print('sharper polynomial',t,j,c,p,q,loss.b)
if __name__=='__main__':certify_refine()

Let \(a=1-\beta\), \(H_*=3000175332800\), \(h_*=\log H_*\), and \(T=e^{u/2}/6\) in FKS Theorem 3.2, as in candidate.md. Put \(s_0=.72\) (mesh branch) or .745 (continuous branch). Dusart 2.3 applies already at these lower splits: with \(p=8(1-s)/3, d=1-p, q=5-2s\), use \(A=4.9\,3^p,B=51.5\); the optional second branch substitutes a lawful FKS pair, or keeps the Dusart pair. For the high zero series use the right-endpoint cumulative mesh as in \(Z\), but with spacing \(1/2000\) (final short cell allowed) and \(H_*\) instead of \(H\) in the quartic Taylor mass. Let \(Z_*(u)\) denote its **unscaled** majorant. Both branches include cap atoms. Low zeros and the Perron remainder are bounded by
\[
 (.04u^2+13u+2)e^{-u/2}+.02u^2e^{-(1-s_0)u},
\]
using (B)'s derivation with \(s_0\) substituted, and the **old** \(J\) based on \(H\) (a safe enlargement). This is the cost of omitting low-real-part zeros, not all zeros above \(T\).

For the missing high zeros **above** \(T^\star\), use disjoint real-part cells \([s,t)\) of width \(1/100\) starting at \(s_0\), including the final cap in its cell. The cost per cell is bounded by
\[
 2e^{-(1-t)u}\int_T^\infty
   (A(s)y^{p(s)}(\log y)^{q(s)}+B(s)(\log y)^2)\frac{dy}{y^2}.
\]
We may bound a cell by its cumulative mass without subtracting another upper bound. The product of \(e^{-(1-t)u}\) and \(T^{-d}\) is critical: bounding all cells by the cap at this step is far more costly. With \(v=\log T=u/2-\log 6\), the two terms are bounded by
\[
 \frac{2A\,6^d}{2^q(d-q/v)}\,u^q e^{-(1-t+d/2)u}
 +12B((u/2)^2+u+2)e^{-(1-t+1/2)u}.
\]
Indeed \(v^q\le(u/2)^q\), \((1+w/v)^q\le e^{qw/v}\) and \(\int_T^\infty (\log y)^2y^{-2}dy=(v^2+2v+2)/T\). These are the positive terms \(\kappa_\nu(u)u^{n_\nu}e^{-b_\nu u}\) in `parts`, together with the low/perron terms above. Their prefactors are positive nonincreasing where the checked denominators are positive. This proves the high-series decomposition of candidate.md with the new remainder everywhere on the stated rays. In particular at the used endpoints (lowest mesh start 130) \(T\ge H_*\); the proof does not extend the direct hypothetical \(\psi\) majorant to earlier arguments.

The weighted transfer via (K) consequently gives, for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 L^j |W_j(L)| \le
 \min(1+2(1+j/L)/H_*,\,1+j/(aL)) Z_*(L)
 + \sum_\nu \kappa_\nu(L)L^{n_\nu}e^{-b_\nu L}
 \left(1+\frac{1+j/L}{b_\nu-n_\nu/L}\right).
 \tag{M*}
\]
For each remainder use the decreasing prefactor and \((1+w/L)^n\le e^{nw/L}\) in the integral. The first zero multiplier follows by direct parts as before. For the second put \(f(u)=u^{-j}\), \(\lambda=\rho-1\). The contribution of \(-e^{\lambda u}/\rho\) under (K) is **exactly** \(\int_L^\infty f(u)e^{\lambda u}\,du\): integrating \(f'\) in \(k_j=f-f'\) produces the endpoint which cancels. Multiplying by \(L^j\), one integration by parts gives main term \(e^{\lambda L}/(1-\rho)\) and difference in absolute value at most
\[
 \frac{j\,e^{(\Re\rho-1)L}}{aL|1-\rho|}.
\]
Here \(|1-\rho|\ge|\Im\rho|\), as is \(|\rho|\); the mesh majorizes weights \(1/|\Im\rho|\), not just \(1/|\rho|\). This proves (M*) including the exactly 1 multiplier for \(j=0\). All integrals commute with the high series by absolute reciprocal summability and uniform exponential majorization. For the original proposed limsup, apply this exact calculation and dominated convergence after scaling by \(e^{aL}L^j\); off-cap terms vanish, while the cap mass is bounded by the quartic \(C(\beta)\). The positive remainders and prime power terms tend to zero after scaling and the exponential conversion multiplier tends to 1. Thus the proof does not substitute 1 for a limiting finite-height factor which is actually greater than 1.
